title: every feature tested the same way, every time
summary: The rules of the game did not change; the referee got stricter. Every feature is now in one catalog with the steps that prove it, one command runs the whole stack, and a pull request has to show the evidence for what it touches. Two tokens a joined machine carries lost powers they never needed.

player.title: Player 1: you, with a spare machine
steps: Read the page: free places, the length of the list, how long a place lasts. No account, no e-mail.
Make your own keys. The private halves never leave your machine; you paste only the public ones.
Ask: your browser (or visit.py) solves a small puzzle, the page hands you a claim code once.
Wait: the only place is taken, so you are number 1 in the list, with an estimate of when your turn comes.
Your turn: visit.py wait collects the bundle, sealed to your key. Only your machine can open it.
edge-mesh join: one command, and your machine is a node of someone else's cluster, in your own namespace.
Play: a pod runs on your node. Ask for the cluster's nodes and the answer is 403: you only see your corner.
Game over: the lease ends, the tick expels your node and the tunnel to the API goes quiet.

host.title: Player 2: the host who runs the pool
steps: Open the pool: automatic admission on, one place, a lease per player.
The puller, outbound only, brings the new request from the page; the server never holds a credential.
The tick does the admitting: when the place frees, it approves the first in line and seals its bundle.
kubectl get nodes: the stranger's machine is there, Ready, with the trust public.
The countdown: mesh host leases shows the time left. The host does nothing; the timer will.
Reap: at the end of the lease one tick revokes the node, deletes its namespace and frees the place.

features.name: The Cilium guard
features.what: The Cilium agent's token on a joined node can no longer forge another node's endpoints, WireGuard key or identities.
features.why: A joined node is someone else's machine: its owner can read every token on it. A token should do only what that node needs.
features.command:
make poc-vm      # V06c, V09b-V09c
make poc-golden  # G3.5

features.name: SPIRE, scoped
features.what: The SPIRE agent's token may only get nodes and pods: no nodes/proxy, nothing cluster-wide beyond that.
features.why: nodes/proxy reaches every kubelet. A guest never needs it.
features.command:
make poc-vm      # V103
make poc-golden  # G3.6

features.name: The puller's token
features.what: Normalized on write and read; verify proves the page accepts it, from your host, without sending it to the server.
features.why: A trailing newline used to lock the host out of its own page.

features.name: make regression
features.what: Every suite of the catalog, in a fixed order, each with its own state; it never touches what it did not create, and keeps each suite's logs with secrets redacted.
features.why: Same commit, same host, same day: the same table. A release is that table, all PASS.
features.command:
make regression
make regression ONLY="poc-join poc-revoke"

features.name: docker-vm
features.what: On a host with Incus and no Docker, the Docker and kind suites run inside a VM of the run: nothing is skipped for want of a runtime.

features.name: The gate
features.what: docs/FEATURES.yml maps every path to a feature; a pull request cites the PASS of the suites it touches, says its docs impact, and its diagrams carry the hash of their source.
features.why: Evidence, not promises: a change cannot ship untested or with a stale diagram.
